chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from Ali ibn Al-Salt, from the cousin of Shihab ibn Abd Rabbih, who said:

I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the pains and indigestion I was experiencing. So he said to me: 'Have lunch and have dinner, and do not eat anything between them, for therein is the spoiling of the body.'
Have you not heard Allah, Mighty and Majestic, saying to them: 'Their sustenance therein is morning and evening'?

key_terms.فَسَادَ الْبَدَنِ: Spoiling or deterioration of the body

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on eating frequency and its effect on health?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) prescribes limiting intake to two main meals to prevent bodily decay, linking this physiological wisdom to the Quranic rhythm of sustenance provided 'in the morning and evening' (Surah Maryam 19:62). This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on moderation in eating as a means of preserving health and spiritual clarity, reflecting the natural biological cycles ordained by God.
